aliases: adjunction with invertible unit and counit
T both left and right adjoint of S

evidence.intree_statement: Class AdjointEquivalence {C D : Category} (F : C ⟶ D) (U : D ⟶ C) := { adj_equivalence : F ⊣ U; adj_equiv_unit_iso (x : C) : IsIsomorphism (@unit _ _ _ _ adj_equivalence x); adj_equiv_counit_iso (y : D) : IsIsomorphism (@counit _ _ _ _ adj_equivalence y) }.

Definition AdjointEquivalence_swap_adjunction `(A : @AdjointEquivalence C D F U) : U ⊣ F — via AdjointEquivalence_swap (line 407): the two adjoints trade places, i.e. the right adjoint is simultaneously a left adjoint (the book's 'T is at once left and right adjoint of S')

Definition AdjointEquivalence_to_counit ... : F ◯ U ≈ Id[D] (and AdjointEquivalence_to_unit, line 388) — the componentwise iso witnesses assemble into the natural-isomorphism cells, confirming the definition means natural isos of the unit/counit

statement_record.book: An adjoint equivalence is an adjunction <T, S; eta, epsilon> in which both the unit eta : I ≅ ST and counit epsilon : TS ≅ I are natural isomorphisms; then <S, T, epsilon^{-1}, eta^{-1}> is also an adjunction, so T is simultaneously left adjoint and right adjoint of S.
statement_record.intree: AdjointEquivalence F U: a hom-setoid adjunction F ⊣ U with IsIsomorphism witnesses for every unit and counit component; AdjointEquivalence_swap_adjunction produces the reversed adjunction U ⊣ F.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — componentwise invertibility of unit/counit is equivalent to the cells being natural isomorphisms (the file assembles the natural-iso cells from the witnesses, their coherence being unit/counit naturality); the both-sided-adjoint rider is delivered by AdjointEquivalence_swap_adjunction.

verifier.notes: Blind pass independently reached PRESENT with the same citations. All quotes verified verbatim: Theory/Equivalence/Adjoint.v:69-75 AdjointEquivalence (three fields as quoted), :414-416 AdjointEquivalence_swap_adjunction : U ⊣ F built from AdjointEquivalence_swap at :407-410, :379-385 AdjointEquivalence_to_counit and :388-394 AdjointEquivalence_to_unit. The strength_comparison's key claim is sound and I checked it rather than assuming: componentwise IsIsomorphism witnesses do assemble into the natural-iso CELLS, via IsIsoToIso plus adjoint_equiv_counit_coherence/adjoint_equiv_unit_coherence (:348, :364), whose proofs are exactly unit/counit naturality — so the class really does mean the book's 'eta and epsilon are natural isomorphisms'. File is registered in _CoqProject. ONE UNSTATED RIDER, not enough to downgrade: the book identifies the reversed adjunction's unit as epsilon^{-1} and its counit as eta^{-1}. In-tree, AdjointEquivalence_swap routes through EquivalenceOfCategories_sym and Equivalence_to_AdjointEquivalence, which rebuild the transposes from equiv_adj_to/equiv_adj_from; nothing proves that the resulting unit is the inverse counit. rg over Theory/Equivalence/Adjoint.v finds no such identification. The mathematical content the book is after ('T is at once left and right adjoint of S') is delivered; only the componentwise identification of the swapped cells is missing.

aliases: full + faithful + essentially surjective iff equivalence

evidence.intree_statement: Theorem FF_ESO_Equivalence `(F : C ⟶ D) `{@Full C D F} `{@Faithful C D F} `{@EssentiallySurjective C D F} : EquivalenceOfCategories F. — (iii) ⇒ (i)

Theorem Equivalence_Faithful `(E : @EquivalenceOfCategories C D F) : Faithful F (171); Theorem Equivalence_Full ... : Full F (214); Theorem Equivalence_EssSurj ... : EssentiallySurjective F (221). — (i) ⇒ (iii)

Theorem Equivalence_to_AdjointEquivalence `(E : @EquivalenceOfCategories C D F) : AdjointEquivalence F (@quasi_inverse C D F E). — (i) ⇒ (ii), carried by the same functor and quasi-inverse, exactly MacLane's (iii)⇒(ii) construction route (universal arrows from fullness+faithfulness+eso)
Definition AdjointEquivalence_to_Equivalence `(A : @AdjointEquivalence C D F U) : EquivalenceOfCategories F. — (ii) ⇒ (i)

statement_record.book: For S : A -> C the following are equivalent: (i) S is an equivalence of categories; (ii) S is part of an adjoint equivalence <T, S; eta, epsilon>; (iii) S is full and faithful and each c in C is isomorphic to Sa for some a (proof of (iii)⇒(ii) by choosing T_0 c and eta_c : c ≅ S(T_0 c) and invoking universality).
statement_record.intree: The full cycle in both directions: FF_ESO_Equivalence ((iii)⇒(i)); Equivalence_Full/Equivalence_Faithful/Equivalence_EssSurj ((i)⇒(iii)); Equivalence_to_AdjointEquivalence ((i)⇒(ii)); AdjointEquivalence_to_Equivalence ((ii)⇒(i)).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — all three nodes with both directions. Presentation difference: Full and EssentiallySurjective are split, choice-carrying classes (chosen prefmap preimages, chosen eso_obj/eso_iso witnesses), so (iii)⇒(i)/(ii) is choice-free where MacLane's existential reading invokes AC to choose T_0 c and eta_c — the constructive kernel, disclosed in the Theory/Equivalence.v header (HoTT-book style). Under the book's classical reading the statements coincide.

verifier.notes: Blind pass independently reached PRESENT with the same four citations, and the cycle does close in both directions through all three nodes. All quotes verified verbatim: Theory/Equivalence/FullFaithful.v:160-166 FF_ESO_Equivalence ((iii)⇒(i)), :171 Equivalence_Faithful, :214 Equivalence_Full, :221 Equivalence_EssSurj ((i)⇒(iii)); Theory/Equivalence/Adjoint.v:333-341 Equivalence_to_AdjointEquivalence ((i)⇒(ii)) and :398-402 AdjointEquivalence_to_Equivalence ((ii)⇒(i)). Both files registered in _CoqProject. The choice caveat in strength_comparison is accurate and matches the in-file disclosure (Theory/Equivalence.v:102-117: EssentiallySurjective is split into chosen eso_obj/eso_iso precisely because the classical form needs AC, and FF_ESO_Equivalence invokes no choice principle). ONE INACCURATE GLOSS, in the evidence note for Equivalence_to_AdjointEquivalence only, not in the classification or the statement_record: it says the proof is 'exactly MacLane's (iii)⇒(ii) construction route (universal arrows from fullness+faithfulness+eso)'. The file header at Theory/Equivalence/Adjoint.v:26-33 says the opposite — 'The route is direct — it does not rectify one of the two comparison cells through the triangle identities' — and builds the hom-setoid transposes outright from prefmap and eso_iso; no universal arrow is constructed. The logical content of the arrow ((i)⇒(ii), which with FF_ESO_Equivalence composes to (iii)⇒(ii)) is right; only the description of the proof technique is wrong. Not grounds to overturn.
